Maya R: Heads-up — marketing is running the spring campaign starting next Tue. Sim I ran shows a 1.6x increase in shoulder-token load during 18:00-21:00 PDT. Need quick headroom check and mitigation suggestions.
Samir K: Do you have peak tokens/sec and concurrent reqs from the sim?
Maya R: Peak tokens/sec ~ 480k, sustained shoulder ~ 320k. Concurrent requests bumped from ~9k to ~14k in the scenario.
Linh T: Quick sim output I just pulled: ```
{
  "baseline_tokens_sec": 200000,
  "shoulder_tokens_sec": 320000,
  "peak_tokens_sec": 480000,
  "median_seq_len": 75,
  "kv_cache_hit": 0.62
}
```
Linh T: With current GPU mix (A100-p4-equivalent) our measured tokens/sec per-GPU ~ 55k for the workload distribution, so naive GPU count = ceil(480k/55k)=9.
Felix G: That's 9 GPUs at peak. Current cluster autoscaler target has 6 reserved for this pool -> shortfall 3 GPUs.
Priya S: Also seeing noisy network drops in us-west during the same hours last week — packet loss 0.2-0.5% on average, spiking to 1% for a few mins. That compounds batching and increases retries.
Maya R: Do we have a model for how packet loss maps to effective throughput loss?
Samir K: Observed rule-of-thumb: ~0.5% loss -> ~8-12% throughput degradation for our RPCs due to retry/backoff and KV cache refill miss rates. At 1% it can be 20%+.
Linh T: I ran a quick sensitivity: if we degrade tokens/sec per-GPU by 12% (worst-case shoulder), effective per-GPU = 48k -> peak GPUs needed = ceil(480k/48k)=10.
Maya R: So with network noise we may need +1–2 GPUs beyond the naive calc. Cost hit?
Felix G: Rough GPU-hours: extra 2 GPUs * 3 hours/day * 7 days = 42 GPU-hours for the week window. At our committed rate that's ~ $630 (ballpark).
Priya S: Short-term mitigations: route 30% of shoulder traffic to eu-west where packet loss is low, enable aggressive prefix-warming for hot keys, and bump autoscaler headroom.
Samir K: Proposed autoscaler tweak: set min_pool=8, target_util=0.65 -> allow faster scale + keep 2 spare GPUs for headroom. Also temporarily raise burst_capacity to +2 GPUs for campaign window.
Maya R: How risky is cross-region routing? Latency spike for EU-routed requests might affect tail latency SLAs.
Linh T: We can route only low-latency-tolerant routes (batch & non-LLM-chat). For chat flows, keep local but use warmed cache and batcher tuning.
Felix G: Ops checklist I can action: 1) Apply autoscaler change (Samir/TODO) 2) Add ephemeral 2-GPU burst pool for Tue–Thu 18:00-21:00 PDT 3) Deploy prefix-warm job 1 hour before window 4) Add packet-loss alert on us-west 0.3% sustained for 5m.
Samir K: I'll post the autoscaler PR now and tag infra oncall. Command I used for the sim: ```bash
python infra/sim.py --scenario spring_campaign --scale 1.6 --net-loss 0.005
```
autoscaler-bot: @Samir K created PR #482: autoscaler: shoulder headroom + burst-capacity (link) :shipit:
Priya S: I'll put a quick NOC runbook: if us-west packet-loss >0.6% -> traffic-shift policy A (30% eu shift) and escalate to network team.
Maya R: Thanks — plan sounds good. Can we reconvene Mon 10:30 to lock the exact GPU-hours and cost approval?
Felix G: Yep, sec — I'll attach a short cost spreadsheet before the meeting. :thumbsup:
Samir K: oncall pinged. I'll include simulation outputs and assumptions in the PR.
Maya R: Great, appreciate the quick triage.
Priya S: looping @network-team for visibility.
Linh T: added a note to the model: assume kv_cache_hit degrade of -0.08 per 0.5% net loss (so we can tune warming).
Maya R: End of thread for now — will follow up with the meeting invite. :calendar:
